clue.text: Female bobcat: her inelegance shows

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display inside the words bobcat, her and inelegance

explanation.surface: A female wildcat moves so clumsily that her lack of grace is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female bobcat' reads as one description, but 'Female' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female by example.

clue.text: Comes over on time, most annoyed

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: comes over, as in goes across, means crosses

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late becomes extremely irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is a synonym of angry, so the superlative means angriest of all.

clue.text: Little daughter pursuing volunteers

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the daughter's letter comes after

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A small girl runs after a group of volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, as in 'a little', is an informal synonym for a small bit.

clue.text: Each navy's merits

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, with the S from the possessive

explanation.surface: Every sailor's good qualities are listed.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it through effort, a synonym of gaining it by work.

clue.text: Poor internet media of uncertain value

indicators.note: poor suggests something done badly, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Low-quality online media is of questionable worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indeterminate has not been fixed or measured, so its worth is unknown.

clue.text: Urges former host briefly to accept empty river-boat

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: to accept means the shortened word takes the next letters inside it
briefly means the word host is cut short by its last letter
empty means the word river-boat loses everything but its outside letters

explanation.surface: A past host is pushed to take an unoccupied riverboat on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts RT (the outside of river-boat) inside HOS (host without its T).
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to strongly encourage, a synonym of pressing someone to act.

clue.text: Note that conveys annoyance

definitions.meaning: in the sol-fa scale, the first note is spelt this way in British usage
an exclamation of frustration, popularised by Homer Simpson

explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both a sol-fa note and a cry of exasperation.

clue.text: Director initially phases in new academic posts

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of Director
new means the letters of phases in are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A head of department gradually brings in fresh university roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean heads a faculty, and the role itself is held as a university office.

clue.text: Wall that's sunk for a bit of a laugh?

definitions.meaning: a sunken boundary in a ditch, used on estates so the view stays open
written laughter, as in a chuckle in a comic strip

explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a wall set in a ditch on English country estates, keeping livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken garden wall and the sound of laughter share this spelling.

clue.text: Sent for and told what to do

definitions.meaning: requested goods, as in placed a request with a shop
commanded, as an officer instructs a soldier

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both requested by purchase and commanded with authority.

clue.text: Fellow at hotel is former PM

parts.note: a fellow is a male, referred to as he
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man staying at a hotel turns out to be an ex-prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was the British Conservative prime minister from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Eastern rulers unaltered by move to west

definitions.note: the kings of Persia, the definition doubling as the word that reads the same both ways

indicators.note: in an across clue, moving west means reading right to left, and the word stays the same that way

parts.note: the kings of Persia, the definition doubling as the word that reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Monarchs of the East stay the same despite relocating westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Shahs were the hereditary monarchs of Iran, an example of rulers from the East.

clue.text: Coming to a boy perhaps in a part of prison building?

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the prison section

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name, given as an example

explanation.surface: Is someone about to approach a lad in a prison wing?
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, so the noun is the process of waking up.

clue.text: Flighty singer with the short career

indicators.note: short means the word the loses its last letter

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: A capricious vocalist has a brief professional life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for a job but is the verb, to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, and a singer that flies is fairly called flighty.

clue.text: Accommodation that is for camp-anologists?

parts.note: campanologists ring bells, and split as camp-anologists they become campers too, so their shelter is a conical canvas one

explanation.definitionFit: A bell tent is a cone-shaped tent with a single pole, shelter for campers.

clue.text: Good fellow offers to recruit for English county

parts.note: a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST
to afford is to give or offer
to hire is to take on staff

explanation.surface: A decent man proposes taking someone on for a county in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands, known for its potteries.

clue.text: Trivial stuff editor made a mess of

explanation.surface: An editor botched some lightweight content.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff a task, such as lines or a catch, is to bungle it.

clue.text: Menuhin, happy at last, his daughter regularly returning

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of happy
returning means those alternate letters are read backwards
regularly means every other letter of his daughter is taken

explanation.surface: The violinist Menuhin is pleased when his daughter keeps coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes IDUHE (the even letters of his daughter) and 'returning' turns it to EHUDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Yehudi Menuhin was the celebrated violinist, so his surname clues his first name.

clue.text: Facility, initially lamentable, that artist uses

parts.note: facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of lamentable

explanation.surface: A painter's amenity starts off poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter rests the canvas on a wooden stand while working.

clue.text: Boy or girl's name turning up in lists, illegible

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A unisex name appears in some hard-to-read registers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the letters bottom to top; no word signals the hiding, which the reversal implies.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis is a given name used for both sexes, as well as a surname.

clue.text: Mark for good spelling, chemistry and reading: first in each

indicators.note: first in each means take the opening letter of every following word

explanation.surface: A school report's grade for spelling, chemistry and reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark for good' looks like a school grade, but means a permanent mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a blemish left for ever on the skin, a lasting mark.

clue.text: Stony-faced chap?

parts.note: a man's name that is also a rock face, so a chap with a stony face

explanation.definitionFit: Cliff is a man's name and also a steep rock face, hence stony-faced.

clue.text: Free lager? Ta awfully!

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done terribly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grateful drinker is offered beer on the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner at large has escaped and is not confined, so is loose.

clue.text: Caviar that's rank, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a rank is a row, as in a line of soldiers

explanation.surface: Fish eggs that smell off, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective for bad caviar but is the noun, a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is the salted eggs of the sturgeon, a type of fish eggs.

clue.text: Kid's charity event

definitions.meaning: British students hold an annual fundraising week of stunts called ... week

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to tease and is also a student fundraising event.

clue.text: Settee hid unusual list of things to eat

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of settee hid are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A sofa concealed a strange item.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet plan written down gives the foods allowed, so it is a menu for slimmers.
